_comment: Written by the trading runs (9:30a / hourly / 3:30p ET). Never contains account numbers, broker IDs, or any account other than the sandbox.

account.note: Cash account, and flat. The broker returns no equity positions and no option positions, so the entire balance is cash and all of it is settled. The 121.52 that sat unsettled overnight has cleared on the T+1 cycle, which is why deployable moves from 4.54 to 126.06 rather than by any funding event. This file was wrong until this run: it described 4 UPST held overnight, and those shares were sold at 30.3801 at 15:38:23 ET on 8/5, 84 seconds after the pre-close run read the book. The retro caught it, flagged state.json as stale rather than editing a file it does not own, and this is the run that owns it. Deployable of 126.06 buys a share of every name on the list except LEU at about 190, and for the first time it is also enough to pay for an option contract - which turns out not to matter, because the spread ceiling rejects them anyway.

entryWatch.trigger: Buy limit 9.75 or better while 9.505, the 8/5 high, holds as support
entryWatch.why: Published as today's specification, and forced on item 1. NuScale reported 8/5 after the close at -0.13 against a -0.13 estimate, exactly in line, and an in-line EPS at a pre-revenue reactor developer does not answer 'why does this move meaningfully, soon'. What earns the entry is item 5 rather than item 1. Of the four names that printed last night this is the only one being bought: it opened 9.30, below its own 9.38 close, flushed to 9.19 in the first minutes and has since made three consecutive higher 5-minute closes - 9.5008, 9.5298, 9.58 - through the 8/5 high of 9.505, with volume accelerating into the third bar at 454K after 308K. Bid 9.70 at 09:47, +3.4%. A print that opens red and gets bought all morning is the opposite of the crowded-bulls setup item 5 warns about. The risk being taken deliberately: this is a day-1 reaction bar rather than the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook prefers, and the name is roughly a third above the 7.21 it printed on 7/17.

entryWatch.trigger: A hold above the 8.20 session high after the first hour
entryWatch.why: The best chart on the board and the second-ranked candidate, held back on tape rather than on structure. JOBY took out its 8/4 high of 8.10 this morning at 8.20, which is a genuine breakout, and it did it on a print the market liked despite an EPS miss - -0.25 against a -0.23 estimate - which usually means the report's substance was elsewhere. Against that: the 5-minute bars are 8.175, 8.08, 8.08 on 590K, 260K, 210K, so the breakout faded and did so on declining participation. It carries the same item-1 problem as SMR with a worse version of the fact pattern, because here the one hard number available actually missed. It is also about 22% above the 6.63 it printed on 7/29, a 52-week low set six sessions ago. Reconsider if it closes the hour above 8.20 with volume back.

The best catalyst on the board on the numbers and the clearest illustration of why item 1 alone is not enough. IONQ beat by a wide margin - -0.33 against a -0.60 estimate, about 45% better - and the tape is selling it: opened 41.37, low 40.17, bid 40.98 at 09:47, still below the open. A 45% beat that cannot hold its opening print is a beat the market has already decided about. Two further reasons it was not the pick: at about 41 a share the account can hold 3, and a -8% stop is 3.28 of room in a name that ranged 1.38 in its first fifteen minutes, so the stop sits inside the noise. Wait for the reclaim rather than buy the fade.

entryWatch.trigger: Reclaim and hold of 30.32, the pre-earnings 8/4 close
entryWatch.why: The board's own 8/5 entryWatch wanted exactly this - 'a pullback that holds on 8/6 or 8/7, not today's reaction bar' - and both of the reasons it was marked dead have expired: the account is no longer long the name and no longer has 4.54 to its name. So it got a real look, and it failed on its own terms rather than on the old ones. The 8/5 bar is the problem: opened 34.595, closed 30.20, giving back the entire earnings gap on 12.3M shares against a 5.1M average. That is distribution, not a pullback after strength, and the rulebook's setup list means the latter. This morning did reclaim - 29.21 open, 29.18 low, 30.59 high - but it has since rolled to a 29.94 bid, back under the 30.20 close, on 290K shares against a 5.1M average. A reclaim nobody participates in is not a reclaim. Dead for today; it does not carry forward as this setup.

entryWatch.trigger: None available - item 2 forbids buying the +20% reaction bar
entryWatch.why: Recorded because refusing it is the point. SOUN beat at -0.02 against -0.06 and gapped from a 6.43 close to an 8.045 open, about +25%, which is the single clearest instance of the entry checklist item 2 exists to forbid. It is also already failing: high 8.19 in the first minutes, bid 7.76 at 09:47, so -4.3% from the open on roughly 11M shares in fifteen minutes. This is the same shape as the AMD 8/4 entry this project graded 0/6 - a spike day, bought into strength, on the day the catalyst printed. The mandate obliges an entry somewhere; it does not oblige this one, and a forced entry is a compromised thesis rather than a compromised instrument.

candidatesAsOf: 2026-08-06 09:47 ET, live session bids read by the open run. The Last column is the official 8/5 settled close.
candidatesNote: Bids are live and quoted as bids, never marks. Deployable settled cash is 126.06 and the account is flat, so for the first time since the rulebook was written this is a real entry list rather than a reading exercise. Four names printed last night - IONQ, SMR, JOBY, SOUN - and the split between them is the whole of today's decision: SMR is bought from below its own close, the other three are being sold from their opens. MARA and RGTI report tonight and OKLO and VST report 8/7 before the open, so all four are no-fly for a five-session hold; a BMO print gaps past every stop. LEU beat by 73% and is the strongest catalyst on the tape, but one share is about 190 against 126.06 deployable, so it is blocked on size rather than on thesis. SMCI reports 8/11 after the close, which falls inside a five-session hold started today.

The only one of last night's four printers being accumulated rather than distributed. About a third above the 7.21 low of 7/17, which is the argument against it.

Ranked second. EPS missed at -0.25 against -0.23 and the stock is up anyway, +4.9% on the bid, which usually means the report's substance was not the EPS line. Took out the 8/4 high of 8.10 at 8.20 - a real breakout - then faded to 8.08 on three bars of declining volume. Best structure on the board, weakest confirmation this morning. 22% above the 6.63 52-week low set on 7/29.

The biggest beat on the board - -0.33 against a -0.60 estimate, about 45% better - and it cannot hold its open. Opened 41.37, low 40.17, bid 40.98, still under the opening print. Also awkward on size: 3 shares is the most the account can hold and a -8% stop is 3.28 of room against a 1.38 first-quarter-hour range.

Beat at -0.02 against -0.06 and gapped 6.43 to an 8.045 open, about +25%. Checklist item 2 forbids this entry outright. Already fading - 8.19 high, bid 7.76, -4.3% from the open on roughly 11M shares in the first fifteen minutes. The AMD 8/4 shape exactly.

No longer held; the 4 shares were sold 8/5 at 30.3801. Gave back the entire earnings gap on 8/5 - 34.595 open to a 30.20 close on 12.3M shares against a 5.1M average. Opened 29.21 today, reclaimed to 30.59, has since rolled to a 29.94 bid on 290K shares. A failed gap plus a reclaim with no participation.
Bid 478.69, -0.7%, a third session of chop under the 8/4 gap-down. No setup, and one share is nearly four times deployable cash in any case.

Beat by 73% - 1.77 actual against a 1.02 estimate - the strongest catalyst on the tape today. Blocked on size, not on thesis: bid 189.78 against 126.06 deployable, so the account cannot buy one share. Recorded so the reason it was skipped is on the record rather than absent from it.
Reported this morning and missed at -0.13 against -0.10. Bid 19.87, about -7.1%. Worth noting against IONQ: the quantum complex is not trading as one thing today.
